title: 1999 AHSME Problem 17
statement: Let \(P(x)\) be a polynomial such that when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 19,\) the remainder is \(99,\) and when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 99,\) the remainder is \(19.\) What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 19)(x - 99)?\)

solutions.text:
By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(19) = 99\) and \(P(99) = 19.\) Write \[ \begin{aligned} &P(x) = (x - 19)(x - 99)Q(x) \\ &\quad {}+ ax + b. \end{aligned} \] Then \[ 19a + b = 99, \qquad 99a + b = 19. \]

Subtracting gives \(80a = -80,\) so \(a = -1\) and \(b = 118.\) The remainder is \(-x + 118.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Dividing by a quadratic leaves a remainder of the form \(ax + b\)
